steps: Extend your non-dominant hand in front of you, palm facing up with the fingers together.
Form your dominant hand into an X: a fist with the index finger bent at the knuckle.
Hold the X hand above the open palm with its own palm facing back toward you.
Tap the bent index finger down onto the palm once with a short, sharp motion.
Keep your face neutral and the base hand perfectly still during the tap.
tip: Lifeprint teaches TAX as one meaning of the COST sign — the same tap also covers fee and fine.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat and steady in front of your chest, palm facing down.
Shape your dominant hand flat or slightly bent, palm facing down as well.
Slide the dominant hand beneath the non-dominant hand.
Move the dominant hand downward away from the base hand, showing what lies underneath it.
Keep the base hand motionless while the moving hand travels down.
tip: Lifeprint glosses this sign BELOW-[less_than] — the same production also means 'less than' for amounts.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat and steady in front of you, palm facing down.
Shape your dominant hand flat or slightly bent, palm facing down.
Rest the dominant hand on top of the non-dominant hand.
Move the dominant hand upward away from the base hand, tracing what rises past it.
Keep the base hand still while the moving hand climbs.
tip: Lifeprint's gloss is MORE-THAN — 'above that amount, exceeding, from that point up.' Pairs naturally with BELOW.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand steady in front of you, flat or slightly bent, palm facing down.
Shape your dominant hand bent or flat, palm facing down.
Position the dominant hand above the non-dominant hand.
Bring the dominant hand downward toward the base hand, stopping just short of contact.
Keep your face neutral — the shrinking space shows a smaller amount.
tip: This is the comparison version of 'less' — Lifeprint pairs it with the THAN family (less-than, more-than, equal).

steps: Shape both hands into P handshapes — fists with the middle finger pressing down over the thumb.
Hold both P hands in front of your chest, palms facing forward.
Swing both arms side to side together, keeping the wrists straight.
Use a lively, celebratory bounce in the movement.
tip: Lifeprint's lesson quiz accepts both the P-handshape and Y-handshape versions; many signers twist the wrists instead of swinging the arms.

steps: Flatten both hands, fingers together, palms facing up.
Hold the palm-up hands side by side in front of your waist.
Sweep both hands forward and slightly upward in a smooth arc.
Let the hands settle a little lower at the end, as if laying something onto a table.
Keep your expression open and generous — the sign presents something to someone.
tip: Lifeprint teaches one production for offer, propose, suggest, and recommend; it covers singular and plural alike.

steps: Form your dominant hand into an X — a fist with the index finger bent at the large knuckle.
Hold the X hand beside your cheek with the bent finger pointing backward past your head.
Flex the bent index finger up and down a couple of times.
Keep the hand near your head so the location carries the time reference.
tip: Lifeprint teaches this in the signing notes as RECENTLY — the finger flicking backward like something that just passed.

steps: Hold both hands in front of your chest in loose 5 handshapes, fingers spread.
Angle the thumbs toward each other, one hand's palm facing up and the other's facing down.
Move both hands in small circles, alternating so they pass each other.
Keep the circling smooth and continuous, like people mingling at a gathering.
tip: Lifeprint also accepts an open-A handshape version — both are glossed SOCIALIZE / associate / social / mingle.

steps: Shape both hands into L handshapes, thumb and index finger opened at a right angle.
Bring the hands together so the index fingertips touch in front of your chest.
Pull the L hands apart sideways in one smooth motion.
Add a slight twisting shake of the forearms as the hands separate.
tip: Dr. Bill's pick is the L-hand version — it keeps LANGUAGE distinct from SENTENCE, which uses F hands.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into an L, thumb and index finger held open and steady.
Press the palm of the L hand against the palm of your flat non-dominant hand.
Pull the L hand back an inch or two, dip it downward, then touch the palm again.
Keep the L hand's palm facing the base palm through both contacts.
Use a firm, even rhythm with a serious, neutral face.
tip: Lifeprint glosses this LAW / legal — the same production covers law, principle, and rule.
